verses.text: Trouble for Ariel! Ariel, the city where David camped! Let the years pile up and the feasts come around again.
Then I'll bring trouble on Ariel. There'll be mourning and crying, and she'll be like an altar hearth to me.
I'll camp all around you, post troops to lay siege to you, and build siegeworks against you.
You'll be brought down so low you'll speak from the ground. Your words will mumble out of the dust. Your voice will sound like a spirit speaking from the ground, your words a whisper from the dirt.
But the crowd of your enemies will become like fine dust, and those ruthless people like husks that blow away. It'll happen in a flash, without warning.
The LORD of Armies will come to her with thunder, an earthquake, a huge roar, a whirlwind and storm, and flames of fire that eat everything up.
All those nations fighting Ariel, everyone attacking her and her fortress and crowding in on her, will be like a dream that comes in the night.

It's like a hungry person dreaming they're eating, then waking up still hungry. Or like a thirsty person dreaming they're drinking, then waking up weak and still thirsty. That's how it'll be for all the nations going up against Mount Zion.
Stop and be stunned! Blind yourselves and stay blind! They're drunk, but wine didn't do it. They're staggering, but strong drink didn't do it.
The LORD has poured a spirit of deep sleep over you. He's closed your eyes, the prophets, and covered your heads, the seers.
Every vision has become like words in a sealed book. Hand it to somebody who can read and say, “Read this, please,” and they'll say, “I can't. It's sealed.”
Hand the book to somebody who never learned to read and say, “Read this, please,” and they'll say, “I can't read.”

The Lord said, “These people come close with their mouths and honor me with their lips, but they've moved their hearts far away from me. The reverence they show me is just a rule somebody taught them.

So look, I'll do something amazing among these people, something that will leave them wondering. What their wise people call wisdom will disappear, and the understanding of their clever people will be hidden.”
Trouble for those who bury their plans deep to hide them from the LORD. They do things in the dark and say, “Who's watching us? Who knows what we're doing?”

You've got everything backward! Is a potter just the same as clay? Can a thing someone made say of its maker, “You didn't make me”? Can something shaped say of the one who shaped it, “You don't know what you're doing”?
Won't it be just a little while before Lebanon turns into a fruitful field and that field looks like a forest?
That day deaf people will hear the words of the book, and blind people will see out of the gloom and darkness.
Humble people will find even more joy in the LORD, and the poorest will celebrate the Holy One of Israel.
The ruthless will come to nothing. The mocker will be gone. Everyone watching for a chance to do evil will be cut off,
the people who get someone charged on a word, set traps for the one who corrects them at the gate, and twist testimony to cheat the innocent out of justice.
So the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says about Jacob's family, “Jacob won't be ashamed anymore, and his face won't go pale.
When he sees his children among him, the work of my hands, they'll honor my name as holy. They'll honor the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
People whose spirits wandered off will come to understand, and the ones who grumble will take instruction.”
